newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says forces to leave Iraq when job done.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says forces to leave Iraq when job done.

text.p: Turkey on Wednesday rebuffed calls from Western and Middle Eastern capitals to withdraw its troops immediately from northern Iraq, where they have been fighting separatist Kurdish rebels for the past two weeks.
"Turkish security forces, as with previous operations, will withdraw from northern Iraq when the operation...has reached its targets," the Turkish foreign ministry said in a statement.
More than 10,000 Turkish troops streamed into northern Iraq two weeks ago in pursuit of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use the region as a base to launch raids into southeast Turkey.
The ministry statement said the cross-border offensive was limited and its only target was to clear the region from "terrorist activities", referring to the PKK.
Rebel leader Abdullah Ocalan said the PKK would retaliate against the Turkish military operation with night attacks.

"With the first stage now finished, the guerrillas will take the important second step. From now we will begin night raids. Let us see what is harder, entering or getting out," Ocalan said by telephone on pro-Kurdish MED-TV on Tuesday evening.
He also proposed cooperation with Massoud Barzani, the leader of a Iraqi Kurdish militia allied with the Turkish forces. "Here I am making a call to Barzani, come and let us cooperate," he said.
NATO-member Turkey's Western allies and regional countries have expressed growing concern over the incursion into a Kurdish enclave protected by the West since the Gulf War ended in 1991.
The Iraqi News Agency said Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz discussed "the Turkish invasion of Iraqi territory" with a Russian envoy in Baghdad on Wednesday.
Aziz has accused the United Nations Security Council of failing to take any measures against the Turkish offensive. Jordan has urged Turkey to withdraw immediately.
Turkey's Western allies have also expressed worries and U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan has condemned the incursion, urging Ankara to pull out its troops.
The state-run Anatolian news agency said Turkish troops killed nine Kurdish rebels in the Sarisarilar border region of northern Iraq in clashes on Tuesday.
The agency gave the total PKK dead since the start of the operation as 1,750. Sources close to the PKK say the figures are exaggerated. Ocalan said only 30 rebels had been killed.
None of the figures could be independently confirmed because the operation is being conducted under a strict news blackout.
Turkey mounted a six-week, 35,000-man operation into the Kurdish-held northern Iraqi regions two years ago but failed to achieve its stated aim of clearing the area of the PKK.
